subject: Food Science
title: Flavor Pairing Theory
description: Learn Flavor Pairing Theory in one minute.

hook.text: Chocolate and blue cheese share 73 common volatile compounds. That's why they pair well—they literally share flavor molecules.

buildup.text: Flavor Pairing Theory sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: Flavor Pairing Theory reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: This theory works in Western cuisine but fails in Asian cooking. Indian dishes pair ingredients that share few volatiles.

climax.text: Successful pairing involves contrast—salt and caramel, acid and fat, sweet and bitter.

punchline.text: Shared molecules explain some pairings. But contrast explains others.

quiz.question: Does flavor pairing theory work universally across all cuisines?
options: No—it works in Western cuisine but Indian cuisine uses contrasting, not matching volatiles
